A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe DOM2 and retain matching methods and experiments. All 20 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DOM2 experiments on MPE, multi-agent HalfCheetah and the 3-agent 6-landmark task, including generalization, data-efficiency and hyperparameter results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds low-quality-data evaluations, further baseline comparisons, component ablations, diversity measurements and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: The diffusion policy, residual noise network, DPM-Solver sampling, actor/critic objectives and trajectory-replication procedure are retained. 'Data augmentation' becomes 'data reweighting,' and the two algorithms are combined into one listing, without changing their operations.

E1.justification: v2 adds random and random-medium behavior datasets across the retained MPE, HalfCheetah and 3-agent 6-landmark tasks. This substantially extends evaluation into low-quality training-data regimes beyond v1's four dataset qualities. The environment families and environmental-shift mechanisms are retained.

E2.justification: The original MA-CQL, OMAR and MA-SfBC comparisons remain. v2 Table 4 adds evaluated comparisons with MA-BRAC, MA-IQL, MA-Diffusion-QL, both MA-EDP variants, OMAC, OMIGA, CFCQL, MADIFF and DoF. Appendix A.3 additionally compares MADIFF and DoF across MPE tasks and computational costs.

E3.justification: The data-efficiency plots change from averaging three dataset qualities to five and revise the sample-size grid. The regularization sweep extends from 25 to 100. New protocols include component-removal controls, return-above-400 policy counts, threshold tests and computational measurements over 10,000 training steps with scheduled episode evaluations.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's regularization and diffusion-step sweeps, v2 adds component ablations testing policy improvement, diffusion loss, reweighting and noise-network architecture. Appendix analyses add trajectory visualizations and good-policy counts, reweighting-threshold sensitivity, and data-efficiency comparisons with versus without reweighting.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and report means and standard deviations, with uncertainty already displayed in v1. The existing K=1 and K=10 landmark evaluations are retained. Additional results do not introduce a different uncertainty-estimation practice, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All 48 original benchmark-table result rows are retained unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for new dataset qualities, comparators and analyses. For example, random Predator Prey reports DOM2 at 208.7±57.3 versus OMAR at 14.3±9.5 (Table 1). Table 9 also introduces settings where MADIFF or DoF outperform DOM2. Revised data-efficiency curves use different aggregation and are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the stated score-function definition from -sigma_t times the gradient of log q_t to the gradient of log q_t; Section 4.1 correspondingly calls the network target a scaled score. The substantive diffusion equations and appendix derivations remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain diffusion-based DOM2 with value-guided training and trajectory replication, claiming improved performance, generalization and approximately 20-fold data efficiency. v2 quantifies generalization success as 28 of 30 settings and foregrounds the already-existing decentralized design, without introducing a materially different central claim.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly attributes substantial data efficiency to diffusion itself and additional gains to reweighting, while discussing task-dependent thresholds and automated tuning as future work. Appendix A.3 adds explanations of MADIFF/DoF differences and acknowledges unequal training information and dataset usage. These substantially expand interpretation and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 provides a DOM2 code-access link, specifies dataset mixture proportions previously left unspecified, and documents hyperparameters for the added dataset qualities. It also supplies threshold-selection guidance and explicitly discloses that the main data-efficiency curves omit reweighting. These are reproducibility disclosures; they do not establish that corresponding earlier experiments changed or were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 expands positioning to newer diffusion and offline MARL work, including IDQL, DAC, MADIFF, DoF, CFCQL, OMAC and OMIGA. Sections 2 and 4.4 and Appendix A.3 develop substantial comparisons between DOM2's decentralized policy diffusion and centralized trajectory or joint-policy approaches, beyond v1's mainly single-agent diffusion comparisons.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable. Changes include the title and author information, consistent reweighting terminology, expanded introductory and method explanations, a dedicated ablation subsection, and reorganized appendices. Much of the original prose and mathematical exposition is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds a conceptual schematic, component-ablation charts and trajectory visualizations, and expands the introductory diversity display. It restructures benchmark tables, merges the HalfCheetah tables and the sensitivity figures, adds several analysis tables, and redraws data-efficiency axes and panels. The publication template and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence that was limited in v1: component ablations and direct diversity analyses test why DOM2 works, while broader baseline and low-quality-data evaluations test its comparative value. Dataset-construction disclosures, a code link and computational measurements improve reproducibility and practical assessment. Some superiority language exceeds Table 9, and Appendix A.3 acknowledges comparison confounds, but these qualifications do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
